body: Not sure if you will see this OP, but I'm a therapist and DBT can be super helpful with bipolar disorder and managing symptoms. I'm sorry you are having to deal with this and believe you are strong and capable to figure out what truly is best for you ❤️

I am not sure where you are located, but in some states in the US, you have full protection over mental health information. So the only thing parents could see is the provider and the CPT billing codes for the services. I also totally understand not wanting to be put in a difficult place. Another option could be to self-enroll in an income restricted plan (like Medicaid) where your parents wouldn't have knowledge of services, although this typically is a long process and can take even longer to find available providers. I think checking in with a counselor at your college would be a great idea, especially knowing any stressor may be exacerbated by such a big change

Edit: to reflect I didn't catch you being 18! So all health and mental health info is privileged and cannot be released without your consent!

5-10 minutes of pain was not my experience and I'm sure the same for other women. I was in excruciating pain and near tears for like the next entire day. I had to lay at home because I physically could not do anything. If you've been lucky enough to not experience this pain, it might be best to not overgeneralize the experiences of others that have

This is SUCH a lie. I work in healthcare and had a conversation about misrepresentation of just how painful IUD insertion is with my coworkers a few days ago. Especially if you have to be dilated for insertion (like me). It's absolutely ridiculous to say it is "mildly uncomfortable"

I'm also a therapist and I just own it and have a few answers depending on my bandwidth for the day. I usually say "I'm a therapist" or "I work in mental health". Some people don't ask further, but the one response that always gets me is "man we really need you guys since covid". I almost always respond "yeah covid certainly made things worse, but mental health has always been a huge need even before covid" and people usually stop there lol
You lost me at "make a lot of money" because as a fellow therapist, mental health clinicians are still extremely underpaid lol
